The Atlantic slave trade. This forced migration of an estimated twelve to fifteen million enslaved Africans to the Americas over four centuries became the largest forced population transfer in history. Starting in the fifteen hundreds with Caribbean sugar colonization, it accelerated dramatically as Portuguese, Spanish, British, French, Dutch, and Swedish traders competed while African kingdoms facilitated capture and sale. The horrific Middle Passage crossing lasted six to eight weeks with mortality rates of ten to twenty-five percent. Gradually abolished—Denmark first in eighteen oh-three, Brazil last in eighteen eighty-eight—it created the foundation of systemic racism in the Americas.
